structural_decision.question: zh-CN has one CLDR category; the translator folded the English 'one' arm's {org} into the single 'other' arm. Is the resulting sentence correct Chinese at count=1 and count=12, or does it misstate plurality?
structural_decision.verdict: correct - it does not misstate plurality
structural_decision.detail: Intl.PluralRules('zh-CN').select() returns 'other' for 1, 2 and 12, so all counts render one identical sentence naming blockedTargets[0] and generalising to '任何其他组织'. At count=1 the general disjunct is vacuous (no other org is marked) but nothing false is asserted; at count=12 the named org IS one of the marked, disabled orgs in the same picker, so the sentence is true and more informative than the English. The call site always passes a real name (blockedTargets[0].tenant_name || t('ui.hub.pages.scope.org_unnamed')), so there is no path where {org} is empty. The zh-CN style guide (Plurals) mandates 'other' only and forbids one/other branches, so a 'one' arm would itself be the defect; the English plural_guidance is honoured inside 'other'. The wrong alternative - {org} alone - was correctly avoided: at count=12 it would imply only the named org can enable the feature.
